title: Public baseline-saves recipe (Baseline-BP, -SV, -IP from a clean install)
body:
## Context
Almost every test in this repo loads one of three aged saves: `Baseline-BP` (Bridgeport, Angelista household), `Baseline-SV` (Sunset Valley, Keatons) and `Baseline-IP` (Isla Paradiso, Dregg household on the "Atlantis" houseboat), each aged 14 sim days under DXVK with `keep_alive`, plus copies such as `Cleanup-Test-BP`. They live only on the maintainer's machine and cannot be shared (they contain EA world data). All reference numbers ([PLAN.md Resume here]({{blob}}/PLAN.md#resume-here-updated-2026-10-13-end-of-session), [docs/04 F13]({{blob}}/docs/04-re-findings.md#f13-all-fixes-together-three-worlds-measured-2026-10-12), [docs/05-baseline-results.md]({{blob}}/docs/05-baseline-results.md)) come from them.

Tools exist: `tools/harness/new-save.ts` (fresh save from the menu, deterministic household pick), `tools/harness/age-save.ts` (speed 3, autopilot, `keep_alive`, declines, checkpoints every N days), `tools/harness/save-stats.ts` / `save-sources.ts` (offline save contents).

## Status
Not started. Saves were made by hand-run commands on 2026-10-11/12; the exact command lines are not recorded in one place.

## Task
1. Write `docs/23-baseline-saves.md`: game version (Steam 1.67), required packs, install layer (`node tools/setup/install-fixes.ts install`, default entries), Options.ini, and the exact commands:
   - `node tools/harness/new-save.ts --world "Bridgeport.world" --save Baseline-BP-fresh --household <Name>` (same for SV and IP; find and record the household names the originals used).
   - `node tools/harness/age-save.ts ... --days 14 --checkpoint 1` (record the flags actually needed).
   - How to make `Cleanup-Test-BP` (copy of `Baseline-BP`).
2. Add a fingerprint step: `node tools/harness/save-sources.ts Baseline-BP-fresh Baseline-BP` and record the expected ranges (SimDescription, Relationship, MiniSim counts, save size) so a contributor can see whether their save is "close enough" (aging is not deterministic).
3. Optional: a `tools/harness/make-baselines.ts` wrapper that runs all three in one go.

## How to test
Follow the recipe on a clean user folder (back up yours first), then run `node tools/harness/milestone.ts --worlds bp --runs 1 --minutes 10 --label recipe-check` and compare with [the PLAN results table]({{blob}}/PLAN.md#resume-here-updated-2026-10-13-end-of-session).

## Acceptance criteria
- A contributor can produce all three saves without asking anything.
- `save-sources.ts` counts of the recreated `Baseline-BP` within ~25% of the reference (Relationship ~600, SimDescription ~264, save ~33 MB).
- Sim iterations/s of the recreated save within ~20% of the reference on similar hardware.

## Risks / notes
- Aging is random; numbers will differ. The recipe must say which numbers are expected to vary.
- Never upload saves or world files.

## Verified vs inferred
- Save names, worlds, households and sizes: [verified] (PLAN, docs/09 §6).
- That a recreated save behaves close enough for A/B work: [inferred], this issue measures it.

---
_Shared rules: back up `Documents/Electronic Arts/The Sims 3/Saves` first; change one thing at a time and compare in one load with runtime switches (`profile-world.ts --ab`) where possible; stop on any crash or obvious error and triage it (`node tools/harness/crash-ledger.ts triage`); a 10-min run passes when stuck Sims are no worse than the same world without the change and at most one was caused by a shortcut; tag every claim [verified], [measured], [community] or [inferred]; update PLAN.md ("Resume here") in the same PR as the result; never commit EA game files. Setup: [docs/02 install guide]({{blob}}/docs/02-baseline-install-guide.md); test saves: issue "Public baseline-saves recipe"._

title: Contributor onboarding: portable paths, setup guide, probe/harness quickstart
body:
## Context
The repo was built on one machine. Some tools assume its layout:
- `native/ts3native/build.cmd` calls `vcvars32.bat` from a fixed Visual Studio 2022 **Professional** path.
- `tools/setup/build-fixes.ts` uses the .NET Framework `csc.exe` and reference DLLs from `game-copy/assemblies` (made by `tools/extract-assemblies.ts`).
- PLAN.md and some docs mention a backup drive and Steam paths.
- The game user folder is found through `TS3_USER` or `Documents\Electronic Arts\The Sims 3`; the game folder through `TS3_BIN` or the Steam default.

The test loop is in [PLAN.md Resume here]({{blob}}/PLAN.md#resume-here-updated-2026-10-13-end-of-session) ("How we test", "Working notes") and the tool table in [PLAN.md Tools (all in the repo, Windows)]({{blob}}/PLAN.md#tools-all-in-the-repo-windows).

## Status
No CONTRIBUTING guide. No check that a fresh clone can build.

## Task
1. `build.cmd`: find Visual Studio with `vswhere.exe` (any edition with the C++ x86 tools); fail with a clear message if missing.
2. Grep the repo for absolute paths and machine-specific values (`C:\\`, `D:\\`, user names); replace them with env vars or `%LOCALAPPDATA%`-style defaults, or move them to a git-ignored local config.
3. Write `CONTRIBUTING.md`: prerequisites (Steam game + all packs, Node >= 22.18, Python 3 + Frida 17, VS 2022 C++ x86, .NET Framework 4 csc), first-time steps (`extract-assemblies.ts`, `install-fixes.ts install`, `build-fixes.ts`, `build.cmd`), the run loop (`cycle.ts --restart`, `ts3probe.py serve --launch`, `cycle.ts --save`), the rules (one change at a time, in-load A/B, repro per fix, verified/inferred tags, never commit EA files), and how to report a result (PLAN.md update + data under `docs/data/`).
4. Add a "first run" smoke test section: `node tools/harness/tests-be.ts --self-check`, `node tools/harness/milestone.ts --self-check`, `node tools/setup/content-health.ts --self-test`, `native\ts3native\out\selftest.exe`.

## How to test
Fresh clone on a second machine (or a new Windows user): follow CONTRIBUTING.md only, reach "Baseline-BP loaded in live mode with the probe attached".

## Acceptance criteria
- No absolute personal paths left in tools or docs (except as examples marked as such).
- `build.cmd` works on VS Community and Professional.
- A newcomer reaches live mode with the probe without asking questions.

## Risks / notes
Do not change tool behaviour while doing this; paths only.

## Verified vs inferred
Hard-coded VS path and csc/game-copy dependency: [verified] in the files above.

title: CI on GitHub Actions: build ts3native, run self-tests, type-check tools (no game files)
body:
## Context
- `native/ts3native` builds with MSVC x86 (`build.cmd`: `ts3native.asi`, `selftest.exe`, `decompress-test.exe`, `waterjps-test.exe`) and runs `selftest.exe`. `selftest.exe` and `decompress-test.exe`'s synthetic part need no game files; `waterjps-test.exe` copies code pages from `TS3W.exe` and **cannot** run in CI ([docs/15 Phase 9 offline results]({{blob}}/docs/15-native-patches.md#offline-results-2026-10-13-i7-11800h-32-bit-o2-build-measured-2)).
- `mods/ts3fixes` and `mods/ts3agent` compile against the game's own assemblies (`game-copy/assemblies`), which must never be published.
- Node tools have self-checks: `tests-be.ts --self-check`, `milestone.ts --self-check`, `content-health.ts --self-test`, `tools/github/create-issues.ts --dry-run`.

## Status
No CI.

## Task
1. `.github/workflows/build.yml` on `windows-latest`: checkout, `ilammy/msvc-dev-cmd` (arch x86) or vswhere, build ts3native (same flags as `build.cmd`), run `selftest.exe`; upload `ts3native.asi` as an artifact.
2. Node 22 job: run the self-checks above and `node --check` / a type-strip check on every `tools/**/*.ts`.
3. C#: investigate a compile check **without** EA assemblies. Options: (a) skip in CI and document; (b) hand-written stub assemblies with only the members we call (our own code, no EA metadata copied; check the licence question first); (c) a syntax-only check (`csc /t:library` with missing refs fails, so likely not useful). Write the finding in the PR.
4. Make `build.cmd` usable from CI (see issue "Contributor onboarding").

## How to test
Push a branch; the workflow is green; break a self-test on purpose and see it go red.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every PR builds ts3native and runs `selftest.exe`.
- Node self-checks run.
- C# decision documented (stubs or skipped, with the reason).

## Risks / notes
Never put `TS3W.exe`, game DLLs or decompiled EA code in the repo or in CI caches.

## Verified vs inferred
Which tests need game files: [verified] from `build.cmd` and the test sources. Stub feasibility: [inferred].

title: Multi-laptop test farm: job queue for game runs
body:
## Context
Game tests are serial and slow (launch ~55 s, load ~37-110 s, 10-min profiles, 3 worlds). The harness is already scriptable end to end: `cycle.ts --restart`, `ts3probe.py serve --launch`, `cycle.ts --save`, `profile-world.ts`, `repro.ts`, `tests-be.ts`, `milestone.ts`, and every run is logged in `docs/data/change-ledger.jsonl`. Results land in `probe-out/` (git-ignored).

## Status
Idea only.

## Task
Design (doc first, then a minimal version):
1. Job format: JSON `{commit, install entries + ini overrides, save, command (repro/profile/milestone), switches}`.
2. Runner: a Node script on each test laptop that pulls a job (from a GitHub issue label, a shared folder or a small queue), checks out the commit, builds, installs, runs, and uploads a results bundle (profile CSV/JSONL summary, `/native` + `patches` counters, stuck list, crash triage) as a PR comment or artifact.
3. Hardware fingerprint in every result (CPU, GPU, RAM, driver, game version) so results from different laptops are not mixed silently.
4. Safety: the runner never touches the owner's real saves (own `TS3_USER` folder), restores the install after the job.

## How to test
Two machines run the same `profile-world.ts --tag farm-test --minutes 5` job from the queue and post comparable summaries.

## Acceptance criteria
- Design doc merged.
- One end-to-end job runs unattended on one machine and posts its summary.

## Risks / notes
Game windows need focus (`focus-game.ts`, unfocused drops below 60 fps); a farm machine must not be used interactively during a run. Steam login and EA content stay on each owner's machine.

## Verified vs inferred
All of this is [inferred] design.

title: Allocator cache (ts3native [Alloc]): repeat in-load A/B with --taskstall and a route-fail check
body:
## Context
EA's arena allocator `0x4E5E40` (dlmalloc 2.7 derivative, one `CRITICAL_SECTION` per heap, fastbins only up to 64-byte chunks, unsorted-bin sort on every non-fast Malloc, `malloc_consolidate` before every request >= 512 bytes) is 6.9% of pooled sim-thread samples, 9.9% in Bridgeport, up to 16% with lock waits ([docs/20 Short answer]({{blob}}/docs/20-offload-candidates.md#short-answer)). ts3native 0.8.0 adds a per-thread, per-heap cache of freed 16-1024 byte chunks in front of Malloc `0x4E69D0`, Memalign `0x4E6A20` and Free `0x4E5920`, with heap Shutdown `0x4E5CB0` detoured ([docs/15 Phase 8]({{blob}}/docs/15-native-patches.md#phase-8-per-thread-cache-in-front-of-eas-arena-allocator-v080-alloc-enabled0-by-default)). Source: `native/ts3native/alloc.cpp`. Settings `[Alloc] Enabled=0 Mode=1 ThreadKB=64 MaxMB=4 PerBin=32`; runtime switch `allocMode` (+0x108), probe `/native?alloc=0|1`, `profile-world.ts --ab alloc`.

## Status
Measured once ([PLAN, in-load A/Bs 2026-10-13]({{blob}}/PLAN.md#resume-here-updated-2026-10-13-end-of-session)): BP 10 min, 2-min slices: **on 30.7 vs off 25.7 it/s (+19%), hitches 4.39 vs 6.12/s (-28%), 40% hit rate**. But in the on slices: one 2 s TaskObjects stall and route fail 2.5% vs 1.1%. Not yet default on.

## Task
1. Install: close the game, `node tools/setup/install-fixes.ts install --only native-patches`, set `[Alloc] Enabled=1` in `Game\Bin\ts3native.ini`; log must show `OK   alloc cache: mode 1` and four `OK   detour EA heap` lines.
2. BP: `node tools/harness/profile-world.ts --tag bp-alloc2 --ab alloc --slice 2 --taskstall 250` (10 min). `--taskstall` disables the managed sampler on purpose (two samplers deadlocked the probe).
3. Read the taskstall JSONL (`probe-out/<session>-taskstall.jsonl`): attribute every stall > 250 ms; check whether stalls cluster in on slices.
4. Route fail %: compare on vs off from `profile-compare.mjs bp-alloc2`. If on is higher again, run a 10-min A/B where only the route counters are read, and check whether failing plans differ (same destinations? `RouteBackoff` hits?). A cache cannot change route results unless memory is reused wrongly, so a real difference is a red flag.
5. Repeat on IP (`--tag ip-alloc2`), because IP is route-heavy.
6. Read `alloc cache:` log lines: hits vs misses, `oom 0`, threads, `allocPassedK`.

## How to test
```
node tools/harness/cycle.ts --restart
python tools/probe/ts3probe.py serve --launch      # separate terminal, keep running
node tools/harness/cycle.ts --save Baseline-BP.sims3
node tools/harness/profile-world.ts --tag bp-alloc2 --ab alloc --slice 2 --taskstall 250
node tools/probe/profile-compare.mjs bp-alloc2
```

## Acceptance criteria
- it/s gain >= +10% on BP in two runs, hitches not worse.
- Route fail % on within 0.5 points of off (or a cause found that is not the cache).
- No TaskObjects stall that only appears in on slices; no crash in `ts3native.asi`, `0x4E5E40` or `0x4E51B0`; `oom 0`.
- Then propose `[Alloc] Enabled=1` for the milestone bundle.

## Risks / notes
A game double free is no longer caught and can hand one chunk to two owners ([docs/15 Phase 8 risks]({{blob}}/docs/15-native-patches.md#risks-3)). Up to 4 MB of free memory sits in caches (Error 12 margin). Stop on any heap corruption crash and triage it.

## Verified vs inferred
- Allocator structure and entry points: [verified: decompile].
- +19% it/s, 40% hits: [measured], single run.
- That the route-fail rise is noise: [inferred], to verify.

---

title: Water JPS (ts3native [WaterJps]): Verify=1 run on Isla Paradiso, then in-load A/B
body:
## Context
In Isla Paradiso the water-grid jump-point search `0x620560` is 7.8% of sim-thread samples, ~92% of it in the jump `0x61FE10` that recurses once per cell with ~10 helper calls and two `div`s ([docs/15 Phase 9]({{blob}}/docs/15-native-patches.md#phase-9-faster-water-grid-jump-point-search-v090-waterjps-enabled0-by-default)). ts3native 0.9.0 retargets only the call at `0x6207FB` to `WaterJump`, the same jump as one inlined loop. Offline, `waterjps-test.exe` ran the game's own code against it: **43.9M jumps on 1000 random grids identical (incl. callback calls), 3.9x faster**. Expected ~50 ms/s of sim-thread time in IP, nothing in BP/SV.

Settings `[WaterJps] Enabled=0 Mode=1 Verify=0`; switch `waterJpsMode` (+0x134), `/native?waterjps=0|1`, `profile-world.ts --ab waterjps`. Counters v10: `waterJpsCallsK`, `waterJpsCellsK`, `waterJpsMismatches`, `waterJpsFallbacks`.

## Status
Built, tested offline, **never run in game**.

## Task
1. Add a repro (per the repro rule) that forces water routes on `Baseline-IP`: a boat trip and a swim (`sim_route_to` to a water point / an island lot; add an agent trigger action if none fits). Entry in `tools/harness/repros.json`, e.g. `ip-water-route`.
2. `[WaterJps] Enabled=1 Verify=1`. Log must show `OK   water jps: call 0x006207FB -> WaterJumpHook, mode 1 verify 1, callback 0x0066DC50 inlined`.
3. Run the repro plus 10 min of normal IP play: `waterJpsCallsK` grows, `waterJpsMismatches 0`, `waterJpsFallbacks 0`, no `MISMATCH` lines.
4. `Verify=0`, then `node tools/harness/profile-world.ts --tag ip-wjps --ab waterjps --slice 2` on `Baseline-IP`; compare route ms/s, it/s, hitches.
5. Optional: one A/B with `/simstack` sampling to compare the `0x61FE10`/`0x61FA10`/`0x61F9A0` family share (docs/20 method).

## How to test
```
node tools/harness/cycle.ts --save Baseline-IP.sims3
node tools/harness/repro.ts run ip-water-route --no-load
node tools/harness/profile-world.ts --tag ip-wjps --ab waterjps --slice 2
node tools/probe/profile-compare.mjs ip-wjps
```

## Acceptance criteria
- Verify run: 0 mismatches, 0 fallbacks, no crash.
- A/B: route ms/s in IP lower in on slices (expected ~40-55 ms/s less), it/s not worse, stuck Sims not worse.

## Risks / notes
A wrong jump point changes boat/swim routes (not memory safety). The game's own jump overflows the stack on 1-cell-wide grids; ours passes those to the game unchanged.

## Verified vs inferred
- Hot path and identical results: [verified: decompile + offline test on game code].
- ~50 ms/s gain in game: [inferred].

title: Lot object query cache (ts3fixes spatialcache): repeat A/B and decide the default
body:

Hot callers: tomb-room route callback, local autonomy, parked vehicles, auto lights ([docs/20 4a. Candidate 3 in C]({{blob}}/docs/20-offload-candidates.md#4a-candidate-3-in-c-the-lot-object-query-cache)). Tuning `kSpatialCache` (default False), switch `spatialcache`, counters [62-64].

Small, single run. Known limit: an object created or moved on the lot earlier in the same tick is seen from the next tick.

## Task
1. Check `ts3fixes.applied` lists `Queries.GetObjects: ok` and `Simulator.DestroyObject: ok`.
2. `profile-world.ts --tag bp-spatial2 --ab spatialcache` on BP and `--tag ip-spatial` on IP, 10 min each.
3. Watch ErrorTrap / script error logs for errors that appear only in on slices.
4. Decide: default on if both worlds show >= +3% it/s and no new errors; else leave opt-in and record why.


title: Fewer route plans (routablecache, stuckcheckbusy): night-time A/B over the 3 AM stuck check
body:
## Context
[docs/04a 8. Who plans the routes]({{blob}}/docs/04a-script-layer-stutter.md#8-who-plans-the-routes-measured-2026-10-13): plans are 15.2% of sim-thread script time. Two fixes in `mods/ts3fixes/src/FewerPlans.cs`, both default off:
- `routablecache` (`kRoutableCache`): `Sim.IsPointInLotSafelyRoutable` answers from the SafeSpot verdict cache (0.5 m cell + exact route profile). Counters [65], [66]. Targets 345-456 ms reset stalls.
- `stuckcheckbusy` (`kStuckCheckBusy`): EA's 3 AM `RunStuckCheckHelper.RunStuckCheck` skips Sims held by an object (bed, chair). Counter [67]. Targets a 645 ms stall.

## Status
Daytime in-load A/B: no measurable change (38.8 vs 38.2 it/s, 2.68 vs 2.64 hitches/s) **with no 3 AM check in the window** ([PLAN.md Resume here]({{blob}}/PLAN.md#resume-here-updated-2026-10-13-end-of-session)). The cases they target were never exercised.

## Task
1. Load `Baseline-BP`, set the sim clock to ~2:30 AM (agent time command if present, else add one), then run `profile-world.ts --tag bp-night --ab routablecache,stuckcheckbusy --slice 2 --taskstall 250` long enough to cross 3 AM in both an on and an off slice (repeat on a second night, swapping order).
2. Compare `/taskstall` stalls around 3-4 AM, counters [65]-[67] and the stuck-check reset count.
3. Run repro `bp-idle-unroutable` with `routablecache` on to make sure verdict sharing does not hide stranded Sims.

## How to test
```
node tools/harness/profile-world.ts --tag bp-night --ab routablecache,stuckcheckbusy --slice 2 --taskstall 250
node tools/harness/repro.ts run bp-idle-unroutable --set routablecache=true
```

## Acceptance criteria
- No RunStuckCheck stall > 250 ms with `stuckcheckbusy` on; [67] > 0.
- `routablecache_hits` > plans; no stall > 250 ms in `IsPointInLotSafelyRoutable` callers after warm-up.
- Stuck Sims not worse; then decide defaults.

## Risks / notes
A stale "routable" verdict for up to a sim-day after a wall goes up (same trade as SafeSpot). A Sim frozen in a bed is still caught by `watchdogidle` and Overwatch.

## Verified vs inferred
Shares and stalls: [measured]. Gains: [inferred].

title: IP route adaptor leak on ocean/houseboat portals: run repro ip-portal-leak (fix is default ON)
body:
## Context
In Isla Paradiso persisted `ScriptCore.Route` objects grow 0 -> 62 -> 135 -> 224 over 11 sim days (BP flat). Cause [verified in decompiled code]: `PortalAnimateThroughAction.DoPortal` calls `CreateAdaptors()` and then skips `PerformRoute` for Ocean, Houseboat and some portals, so `ScriptAdaptor.Kill` never runs and `Sim.OnExitReasonsAdded` keeps the adaptor alive ([docs/09 5. Open checks]({{blob}}/docs/09-save-bloat-research.md#5-open-checks)). A stale callback can also consume a `Replan` exit reason so the live route never replans [inferred].

Fix: ts3fixes `PortalAdaptorHook` (`mods/ts3fixes/src/PortalAdaptorLeak.cs`, tuning `kPortalAdaptorLeak` **default True**, switch `portaladaptorleak`, counter [54]). Existing saves: opt-in SaveCleanup part (d) `RunRouteAdaptorCleanupOnce` (counter [55]).

## Status
Built, **shipping default on, never run in game**. This makes it the highest-priority validation in this milestone.

## Task
1. `node tools/harness/repro.ts run ip-portal-leak` on `Baseline-IP` (trigger `sim_portal_trip`, counts `RouteAdaptorCounts`).
2. Same with `--set portaladaptorleak=false`: the leak must show (counts grow).
3. Run SaveCleanup (d) once on a copy of `Baseline-IP` via `reflect_call` and check [55] and that routes still work.
4. Offline: age a copy of `Baseline-IP` 3-4 sim days with the fix on (`age-save.ts`), then `node tools/harness/save-sources.ts Baseline-IP <aged copy>` with `FILTER=Route`: `ScriptCore.Route` flat.

## How to test
```
node tools/harness/repro.ts run ip-portal-leak
node tools/harness/repro.ts run ip-portal-leak --set portaladaptorleak=false
FILTER='Route|Adaptor' node tools/harness/save-sources.ts Baseline-IP <aged copy>
```

## Acceptance criteria
- On: adaptor counts flat across portal trips, [54] > 0; off: counts grow.
- No stuck Sims at houseboats or ocean portals; no script errors.
- `ScriptCore.Route` flat over a few IP days. If the repro fails, set `kPortalAdaptorLeak` to False until fixed.

## Risks / notes
Unsubscribing without `Kill` must not fire `RouteFailed`; the hook is a no-op where `Kill` already ran.

## Verified vs inferred
Leak path: [verified] decompiled `ScriptAdaptor.cs`, `PortalAnimateThroughAction`. Replan side effect: [inferred].

body:

In a dummy process they must detach in reverse load order, or the target crashes at the later unload ([docs/04 F19]({{blob}}/docs/04-re-findings.md#f19-the-per-frame-function-0xec9f00-frame-time-hook-for-test-b-verified-in-ghidra-2026-10-13)). `tests-be.ts` B hooks frames first and lets the profiler detach first. Open; a fix may be in progress locally. Check PLAN.md before starting.

## Task
1. Reproduce: `node tools/harness/tests-be.ts --tag bp-unload --only B` on `Baseline-BP`; capture the crash (`xcpt` report, `crash-ledger.ts triage`).
2. Candidates: CModule still executing on the render thread during unload (needs `Interceptor.revert` + `Interceptor.flush` and a short wait before `script.unload()`); detach order; the probe server's own agent as a third agent.
3. Fix in the harness (not in the game). Add a dummy-process regression test if possible.

title: Route search budget (ts3native 0.4.2 [RouteBudget]): retest now that the detour is cleared
body:
## Context
The world A* `0x676260` has no node or time budget; a failed search expands everything reachable, and retries multiply it ([docs/11-route-planner-re.md]({{blob}}/docs/11-route-planner-re.md)). ts3native 0.4.0 swaps the five cost-function immediates for stubs; past `MaxUs` (100 ms) or `MaxNodes` every edge reads as a wall, so the search fails through its own exit ([docs/15 Phase 4]({{blob}}/docs/15-native-patches.md#phase-4-route-search-budget-v040-routebudget-enabled0-by-default)). Switch `/native?routebudget=0|1`, `profile-world.ts --ab routebudget`.

## Status
**Paused/failed once:** a 10-min BP run with `Enabled=1` had **41 stuck Sims vs 0** without it, with only one search capped ([docs/15 Phase 4 in game (2026-10-13)]({{blob}}/docs/15-native-patches.md#phase-4-in-game-2026-10-13-route-budget-stubs-strand-sims---keep-off)). Code review found the stubs keep cdecl/x87 contracts; two real bugs (clock started before the lock; global budget state) fixed in 0.4.2, not run in game. The suspected `Route_PlanLocked` detour was later **cleared** (`bp-detour2`: 0 stuck, 24,260 plans). So the 41 stuck Sims are unexplained.

## Task
1. 0.4.2, `[RouteBudget] Enabled=1 Mode=0` (stubs installed, budget off): 10-min BP stuck check. If Sims strand with the switch off, the stubs are the cause: bisect by patching one of the five sites at a time.
2. If clean: calibration run `Mode=1 MaxUs=2000000` on `Baseline-IP` 10 min; read `budgetMaxNodesOk` / `budgetMaxUsOk`, confirm `budgetCapped = 0`.
3. Set `MaxNodes` above the measured success maximum; repro `sim_route_to` to an unreachable point (fails fast, Sim controllable), a long legitimate trip (still succeeds).
4. `profile-world.ts --ab routebudget` on BP and IP.

## How to test
```
node tools/harness/profile-world.ts --tag bp-budget2 --minutes 10
node tools/harness/profile-world.ts --tag ip-budget --ab routebudget --slice 2
```

## Acceptance criteria
- Stubs installed + switch off: 0 extra stuck Sims (vs `Enabled=0`).
- On: worst route-stall iterations shorter, route ms/s lower, fail % up only by capped failures, stuck Sims not worse.

## Risks / notes
A reachable destination over the cap now fails; `RouteBackoff` then blocks that unseen townie for 30 sim-minutes. A time cap depends on load; prefer the node cap. "Unseen only" is not decidable natively (`OnlyFlagged` + C# `DebugPathPlan` bit, not wired).

## Verified vs inferred
Stub contracts: [verified review]. Cause of 41 stuck: unknown.

title: Async route planning: routing lock gate, or an own world-level planner (research, paused)
body:
## Context
Route search is the biggest offloadable sim-thread cost (14.5% pooled; BP 97-108, SV 77, IP 184 ms/s). ts3native has: worker offload-sync mode 1 (**stable in game**: 11,523 plans, 46,152 proxied host calls, 0 crashes, **no speed gain** because the sim thread waits) and an async plan (0.5.0-0.7.1) where the Sim's own task sleeps while the worker plans ([docs/18 Async plan (step 2, ts3native 0.5.0 + ts3fixes, built 2026-10-13, not run in game)]({{blob}}/docs/18-route-search-off-thread.md#async-plan-step-2-ts3native-050--ts3fixes-built-2026-10-13-not-run-in-game)).

**Paused** after three root-caused crashes ([PLAN "Async route plan PAUSED"]({{blob}}/PLAN.md#resume-here-updated-2026-10-13-end-of-session)): (1) yield inside a nested invoke (`interp.c:3595`), fixed 0.6.1; (2) host callback `0xD75FA0` clearing the task id on the worker, fixed 0.7.1; (3) heap corruption: the goal step (`Route_PlanCommon 0x7606E0 -> 0x75C2D0 -> 0x63D2F0 -> AStarSearch reset 0x61E320`) runs **outside** the routing lock `world+0x918` on shared lot state, and the A* object Q is one instance for the whole game with a global generation stamp `0x11580C4` and non-atomic refcounts. Thread-private scratch (option B) is a **dead end** ([docs/18 Async plan: thread-private scratch (option B) (2026-10-13, static analysis)]({{blob}}/docs/18-route-search-off-thread.md#async-plan-thread-private-scratch-option-b-2026-10-13-static-analysis)).

## Status
Paused. Current direction: cheaper searches (water JPS, route budget, fewer replans).

## Task (research, pick one)
A. **Routing gate:** the worker takes `world+0x918` for the whole job; every unlocked sim-thread entry into the lot planner takes it too (`0x75C2D0`/`0x63F490`, `0x7929F0`, `0x63F6E0`, `0x633FA0`, `0x634500`, `0x635080`, `0x655EE0`, `0x65E0D0`, `0xC75920`, `0x835110`, `0x835240`, `0xACE4A0`; ~10 small detours). First measure how much sim-thread work between plans does **not** touch the lock (`asyncPumpUs` vs `asyncUs`, `/routelock` probe); if small, stop.
B. **Own world-level planner:** a precomputed lot-to-lot graph plus short local searches (docs/18 rank 7, PLAN "two-level planning"); only for unseen townies; months of work and high stuck-Sim risk.
Write the finding in docs/18 before building anything.

## How to test
Gate prototype: `[RouteAsync] Enabled=1`, `repro.ts run bp-route-async`, then `profile-world.ts --ab routeasync` on BP and IP ([docs/18 How to test in game (serial, saves backed up)]({{blob}}/docs/18-route-search-off-thread.md#how-to-test-in-game-serial-saves-backed-up)).

## Acceptance criteria
A measured estimate of the gain (ms/s) before any build; if built: 0 crashes in 3x 10-min runs, stuck Sims not worse, it/s up.

## Risks / notes
Heap corruption is silent until a crash; use `Verify`-style cross-checks and page heap where possible. Rebuild callers' lock state (`0x657390`, `0xC6BCC0`, `0x63D860` callers) not checked.

## Verified vs inferred

Heavy store content adds ~100 MB; ResourceCache ignores its budget (389-501 MB).

## Status
Pieces measured separately; no single budget.

## Task
1. One table: committed MB and largest free block at menu, after load, after 30 min (test D), for DXVK-only, full stack, full + store content, full + S3PP, with GC heap 40/256/352 MB.
2. Find the smallest GC initial heap that keeps forced GCs near 0 (docs/13).
